title: Exchange Artifact
description: One versioned, self-contained, deployment-agnostic unit of security-operations knowledge. Readers ignore unknown keys, so additive changes need no version bump.

schema_version.description: Bumped only on a breaking change to this envelope.

uuid.description: The artifact's identity. Stable forever — never change it, and never reuse one. Not the path, not the filename, not the git SHA: all three move, and consumers track by UUID.

revision.description: Bump on every change. Consumers compare revisions to decide whether they have work to do; an edit that does not bump is an edit nobody receives.

status.description: Retraction is a state, never a file deletion — a missing file is indistinguishable from a botched merge. 'deprecated' notifies consumers; 'withdrawn' makes them auto-disable it.

status_reason.description: Required when status is not 'active'. Shown to the operator on the consuming deployment.

attack_techniques.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs, e.g. T1110 or T1110.001.

required_fields.description: Raw Wazuh field paths the artifact needs. Generated for search rules — derived from the legs so it cannot drift from what the rule actually does. Do not hand-maintain.

correlation_key.description: The entity the legs bind on. 'none' correlates across the whole organisation.

include_agentless.description: Also match shared-perimeter documents logged against the Wazuh manager rather than a tenant agent.

baseline_lookback_days.description: How far back history is consulted for a novelty constraint.

count_operator.description: 'lte' is an absence firing (a dead-man's switch) and requires correlation_key 'none'.

distinct_field.description: Diversity constraint: the leg is satisfied only when its documents span at least min_distinct values of this field.

novelty_field.description: Novelty constraint: fires on a value not seen within the baseline lookback.

field_name.description: A raw Wazuh document field path, e.g. rule.id or data.srcip.

tests.description: What lets a stranger verify this detection rather than trust it. Samples must be synthetic — they are the likeliest place for real customer data to leak.

subject_slug.description: The incident Subject this playbook responds to, by slug. Resolved on import; the operator picks or creates one if no slug matches.

intended_automation.description: Name only, as free text. Importing deployments deliberately do NOT bind this to their own automation catalog — the step arrives as a manual task naming the intended action, and a human rewires it.

intended_response.description: Name only, as free text. Never bound on import: matching it against a locally autonomous-response-approved entry would hand a stranger's playbook the authority to isolate hosts unattended.
